```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Local programs summarize co-expressed gene modules into phenotypes that can
be mapped as trans-QTL outcomes. The workflow has two steps:

1. `r_hotspot()` detects gene modules from an expression matrix.
2. `transmap_local()` turns each module into one or more program phenotypes.

```{r}
library(transmap)
data(transmap_example)
Y <- transmap_example$Y   # 300 samples x 60 genes
dim(Y)
```

## Detecting modules with Hotspot

`r_hotspot()` is an R implementation of Hotspot for standardized data. It
builds a k-nearest-neighbour graph of samples, tests every gene for local
autocorrelation on that graph, and clusters the autocorrelated genes by their
pairwise local correlations.

By default each sample has `floor(nrow(Y) / 2)` neighbours; set `n_neighbors`
for a more local graph.

```{r}
hs <- r_hotspot(Y, min_gene = 5)
lengths(hs$modules)
head(hs$autocorrelation)
```

Each module is a character vector of genes:

```{r}
hs$modules[[1]]
```

Covariates are not handled by `r_hotspot()`; regress them out of `Y` first if
needed. Genes on the chromosome being mapped should also be removed by the
caller before module detection.

## Building program phenotypes

`transmap_local()` takes the expression matrix and the modules: the
`r_hotspot()` result, or any named list of gene sets.

### WPC (default)

Whitened principal components account for gene-gene correlation that is
expected under the null. The null correlation is estimated from null trans
z-scores (`null_z`, variants x genes). Expression is whitened by it and all
components with eigenvalue above 1 are kept.

```{r}
wpc <- transmap_local(Y, hs, method = "WPC", null_z = transmap_example$null_z)
dim(wpc$scores)
wpc$summary
```

`null_z` may also be given as a list with element `z`, the format of the null
z-score files used in the TransMap pipeline.

### PC1 and aPC

`PC1` keeps the first principal component of each module. `aPC` adds
components while they explain more variance than the Marchenko-Pastur bound
and the cumulative variance is below `max_cumvar`.

```{r}
pc1 <- transmap_local(Y, hs, method = "PC1")
apc <- transmap_local(Y, hs, method = "aPC", max_cumvar = 0.8)
apc$summary[, c("module", "n_used", "k")]
```

### AUCell

`AUCell` scores each module by the area under its gene recovery curve, using
gene rankings of the full expression matrix. It requires the Bioconductor
package AUCell.

```{r, eval = requireNamespace("AUCell", quietly = TRUE)}
set.seed(1)
auc <- transmap_local(Y, hs, method = "AUCell", auc_max_rank = 0.2)
head(auc$scores)
```

### Covariates

With `covariates`, covariates are regressed out of the expression before
programs are built:

```{r}
adj <- transmap_local(Y, hs, null_z = transmap_example$null_z,
                      covariates = transmap_example$covariates)
dim(adj$scores)
```

The columns of `scores` are the program phenotypes to use as outcomes in
fine-mapping or colocalization, for example with `susieR` or `colocboost`.
